ctx.x: Then, in addition, there was your contact with Latin music in New York and I wonder if you could say a little more about that.

Well, every relief band in New York at the time, no matter where you were working. If you were working at a big night club, it was a Latin band. So you had to hear 'em. And, gradually, you heard things that you liked and Machito, he was the first one to actually blend jazz. Because Mario, the trumpet player, he was like the musical

director of the band; he used to be with Chick Webb. He was a trumpet player in Chick Webb's band. So natrually he had that jazz feeling in him. And I know at one time, they were doing the Apollo, Machito, then they would have a jazz saxophonist with 'em. I remember one day, who was that there...I auditioned and Stan Getz auditioned and, I think it was Brew Moore, we all auditioned the same day to do this week in the Apollo with Machito's Latin band. That's how popular the marriage became at that particular time.…
